preconditions.description: k is an integer between 1 and 18 inclusive.
The initial string s has exactly 2^k - 1 characters.

preconditions.expression: all(c in '?01' for c in s)
preconditions.description: Every character in the initial string s is either '?', '0', or '1'.
The number of queries q is between 1 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= p <= 2**k - 1 and c in '?01' for p, c in queries)
preconditions.description: For each query (p, c), p is a valid 1-based index in s and c is '?', '0', or '1'.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly q lines, one for each query.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(int(line), int) for line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each line of output is a valid integer.

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_lines[i] == str(count_possible_winners(s_after_i_queries, k)) for i in range(q))
postconditions.description: The i-th output line is the count of possible winners for the tournament state after applying the first i+1 queries, where count_possible_winners(s, k) returns the number of teams that can win given the game result string s and parameter k.

postconditions.expression: count_possible_winners(s, k) == sum(1 for team_idx in range(1, 2**k + 1) if can_team_win(team_idx, s, k))
postconditions.description: The count of possible winners is the number of teams (indexed 1 to 2^k) for which there exists an assignment of '?' to '0' or '1' such that the team wins the tournament.

postconditions.expression: can_team_win(team_idx, s, k) == exists_assignment(team_idx, s, k)
postconditions.description: A team can win if there exists a valid assignment of all '?' characters in s to '0' or '1' such that the team emerges as the champion following the tournament structure.
